text:
emily_ae: FYI we have a new POC request from LedgerWave (fintech). They require a private deployment, no public ingress, and all egress must be allowlisted (they control firewall). Also need source-ip preservation for their on-prem IDS. Asking: PrivateLink vs TGW/peering, NAT/EIP strategy, ports to open, and a back-of-envelope cost delta vs Dedicated.

carlos_se: quick answers pls for the pre-sales call later today: single account or multi-account? expected RPS and burst? is there a compliance nuance (PCI/PII)?

emily_ae: single AWS account today. Typical ~100 rps steady, bursts to ~500 rps. PCI in-scope, strict logging and KMS. They insist on fixed egress IPs for downstream partners.

lin_arch: high-level guidance: PrivateLink (NLB + VPCE) is the safer path for zero public ingress into their VPC and minimal route table changes. Transit Gateway / VPC peering offers more flexibility and lower network hop counts but increases blast radius and requires CIDR planning.

lin_arch: tradeoffs in one line each:
- PrivateLink: service-facing, per-region VPCE, good for private endpoints, no transitive routing, easier security signoff.
- TGW/Peering: full L3 connectivity, better for many subnets or high throughput, need unique CIDRs and extra security review.

nate_netops: about source-ip preservation: options:
- Preferred: customer hosts an outbound proxy (in their VPC) with a static EIP. We POST to that proxy via PrivateLink or peering and their proxy forwards to on-prem, preserving client IP in X-Forwarded-For (or if they route, the on-prem sees the proxy EIP).
- Alternative: we egress from their VPC (requires us to run components there). NAT gateways will SNAT, so original IP lost unless they route back.
- If they need raw original IPs on-prem, you need asymmetric routing solved (their netops must accept return path).

carlos_se: firewall/ports snippet we can send to them?

lin_arch: minimal egress rules (they asked for copy/paste):

```
# LedgerWave firewall egress snippet for Redwood POC
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: <VPCE subnet CIDR> OR <list of Redwood EIPs>
- Description: Redwood Inference private endpoints / egress
# If using NLB healthchecks, allow TCP 8000-8010 from our control plane IPs to targets (confirm exact port with ops)
```

nate_netops: TLS inspection note: if they perform TLS interception, we need SNI-based routing or provide certificate pinning guidance. With PrivateLink+NLB we can do TLS passthrough. If they require mutual TLS for control-plane calls, that needs cert exchange.

carlos_se: pricing rough ballpark for scoping (not a quote):
- Dedicated: committed GPU pool. Example sizing for their load assuming batching and KV cache: 1x8-GPU pool estimate ~$20k/month (includes reserved infra + Redwood platform charge).
- Private (customer-managed infra): platform license + setup. Typical one-time onboarding fee ~$30k, annual support ~$10k, plus their EC2/GPU costs (visible in their account).

emily_ae: blockers to call out in presales: CIDR overlap, strict no-external-ip policies, and any requirement for an air-gapped control plane. Also note audit/KMS needs.

lin_arch: one more operational pattern to suggest: deploy a small egress-forwarder in the customer VPC (NGINX/http proxy) with an EIP. We send traffic to it over PrivateLink; it forwards out. Pros: customer retains outbound EIP control and full visibility. Cons: adds a tiny appliance to their account.

nate_netops: monitoring/tracing ask: confirm log retention windows and whether they want token-level observability forwarded to their SIEM. This affects both Dedicated and Private options.

billing-bot: reminder: add finance contact for a formal quote; include support tier and any add-on compliance package.

emily_ae: next steps: scheduling 30m handoff with LedgerWave + netops for tomorrow 11am PT. @lin_arch @nate_netops can you join? I'll attach their security questionnaire and a simple network sketch.

lin_arch: I can make 11am PT.

nate_netops: available.

emily_ae: thanks team. I'll collect their preferred static EIP list pre-call and share. :thumbsup:
